review.decision: Reviewed for separate integration from the frozen source; device acceptance remains outstanding
review.notes: This is a truthful retrospective review of work already implemented before main introduced this gate. It does not claim prior review or passing device behavior. Cold and warm actions, real fold and accessibility remain subject to recorded evidence. On 2026-11-05 the cold-action trace exposed drain-before-JS-ack loss; DUO-009 was reviewed before implementing acknowledgement-based retention. Earlier prototype tests remain honestly retrospective. DUO-010 was updated after observing a native drain Promise stall; its non-blocking fallback and foreground recovery are reviewed before implementation. Permission-wait ordering was implemented during diagnosis; its specific regression test was reviewed afterwards and must not be represented as a pre-implementation review. DUO-018 and DUO-019 describe tests reviewed retrospectively after implementation; the new integration review must precede the actual migration. DUO-020 and subsequent driver/suite adjustments are retrospective WIP, not evidence of an earlier review or of a completed fold test. DUO-021 is recorded after its initial WIP implementation; the integration review must precede migration. DUO-022 is recorded after its initial WIP implementation; the integration review must precede migration. DUO-023 is recorded after initial WIP implementation; the integration review must precede migration. DUO-024 and strengthened DUO-010/019 tests are retrospectively recorded WIP; integration review must precede migration. DUO-024 active-state concurrent recovery assertions were added after WIP implementation, pending actual integration review. Duo posture tests wait at most 20 seconds for the measured hinge to reach the requested angle, per the driver 12.20 documentation; screenshots do not alone establish posture. DUO-002 now checks the unique session title after rotation; Duo posture tests wait for a stable observable window or visible modal control frame before asserting state, recorded retrospectively. DUO-025 records the compact navigation preservation fix and regression after WIP implementation; review must precede separate integration. DUO-026 and the DUO-023 outer-panel menu check are recorded after WIP implementation and require review before integration. Integration preparation from PR1810-derived local source cae4c446f3a5cfc8d8cca899d6f7eb9e5aaaf846 onto main 50fd32738d5f5171629a16d1f93e55aedc5d6a4c; this draft is not a review or evidence that original implementation was reviewed in advance. DUO-007 request-diagnostics.test.ts verifies the additional side-channel diagnostics in startFake (mobileapp/e2e/fake-serve/server.ts); the existing CT-HTTP contract remains intact and continues to map startFake. Independent review of frozen Q cae4c446f3a5cfc8d8cca899d6f7eb9e5aaaf846 against B 50fd32738d5f5171629a16d1f93e55aedc5d6a4c concluded with relay c04db94cf9a846c4a2095d3feb0e56c2 after review of earlier source stages and the final delta. The original implementation predates this integration review; this record precedes its separate migration only. Device, candidate and main checks remain outstanding. Follow-up review after run 42047638915: DUO-008 will verify a bounded hosted-only Appium idle lifetime long enough to retain a session during slow simulator preparation, with preparation timing diagnostics. DUO-001 retains its banner-tap assertion and captures the actual system surface when that assertion fails. No product wait or behavior assertion is relaxed; the cause of slow preparation and missing banner remains to be measured. The case objects retain their original reviewed behavior; the separately reviewed diagnostic follow-up above adds evidence without changing those initial acceptance criteria. Follow-up review from a055 simulator evidence: the outer 466pt root contained a 382pt workspace reader and 298pt detail chat because the shell and detail each apply a horizontal safe-area edge. Give each visible screen responsibility for its own outer horizontal inset, protect the regular sidebar and its reveal control separately, and exercise compact and regular state retention. Fold-reading identity must be checked after preserving the visible scroll anchor and revealing the intentionally auto-hidden header; the large-text scenario must navigate from any previous reader back to the list before selecting its session. Preserve all fold, identity, draft, interaction and accessibility assertions. The device remains to be retested. Independent Appium Duo guidance states hinge changes do not select a display and currentDisplayId controls screenshots and W3C actions. The a055 log reset that setting to null after unfolding, then notification long presses targeted the default outer display while screenshots were black. Each independent unfolded Duo scene/rotation case must explicitly measure angle, enumerate displays and select the inner display before actions, retaining all existing behavioral assertions; screenshots and actual native action evidence remain required. Follow-up review of run 42071592214: retain the native SafeAreaView root with no edges so iPad accessibility keeps radar-split visible without reapplying horizontal insets. While a chat reader is away from the live tail, use React Native maintainVisibleContentPosition to keep its first visible turn through content reflow; retain existing live-tail pinning, and verify the actual first visible message across fold. Verify Trace input has the exact intended text before folding, then assert it persists. Preserve all product behavior assertions and keep audit, scene-link and rotation failures visible. Run 42071592214 timed out the complete multi-step Duo rotation journey at Jest 120s while its outstanding WebDriver operation continued into the following scene-link case. Give that complete journey the same bounded 300s budget already used by the fold journey; individual waits, rotation, draft and session assertions remain unchanged. Native driver errors and any true product failures remain failures. In the large-text case, collect both display interactions and attempt each native accessibility audit even if the first audit errors; persist each error and fail the case afterward. Neither audit error nor missing interaction is counted as success. Run 42086224588 delivered a warm scene URL natively but the existing RN one-shot event did not reach JS. For recognized gtmux usage URLs, enqueue each scene delivery with an ID before notifying the visual consumer through a native event; drain and acknowledge once, retry after a missing listener or foreground transition, and keep other URLs on the RN route. Preserve guest/demo rejection and distinct repeated user intents. Native queue/signal checks and a fresh JS event test precede further device validation. Run 42086224588 showed a visible history prompt moved offscreen on fold despite the native anchor. Before width reflow, record a fully visible conversation turn and its viewport offset; restore that turn as its measured layout shifts, cancel on new user gesture, and never interrupt live-tail following or active text selection. Device reflow remains required. The outer accessibility audit also identified a small back hit region; make its measured target at least 44 points without changing its action. Run 42086224588 left WDA reporting the app not running after the warm background transition failed; the next rotation test queried orientation before launching its own app, so it did not execute its journey. Launch that test fixture before capturing orientation, preserve the warm failure and all rotation/keyboard/session assertions, and restore only an orientation actually captured. Conversation turns are windowed and can be replaced while the component remains mounted. When choosing a resize anchor, consider only identities currently mounted so stale measurements cannot steal the anchor after history changes; verify a removed visible candidate followed by a width change. Run 42099308533 warm action reached JS and matched its server but produced neither send result nor server write; the current delegate completion and receipt acknowledgment occur before the asynchronous send completes. Preserve the system response completion and native receipt until the existing quick-reply promise settles, bounded by the existing 20-second background deadline, without retrying an ambiguous send or changing default taps. Test duplicate arrivals while pending and native completion release. This is a correctness fix to premature completion, not a claim that it alone proves the observed failure cause. Run 42099308533 cold URL reached scene but visual tree stayed blank while background state ran. Safe-area-context Fabric source marks the initial insets sent before checking whether its event emitter exists; a missing first event is a plausible gate, not yet directly observed on the device. On iOS obtain a fresh, nonzero-sized current scene window and its actual safeAreaInsets on the main thread before mounting each visual provider, without a static initialWindowMetrics snapshot or fabricated insets. Keep background push active without a scene; retry when the scene or viewport becomes available, preserve fallback for old native shells, and allow subsequent native insets events to update normally. Validate real provider gating with null scene then actual scene and changing insets; separately require the cold Duo device path. Run 42099308533 still lost the visible turn during fold; record only numerical viewport/anchor/layout transitions under the existing test-only debug flag and save them alongside the failing screenshot to determine whether capture or later layout adjustment failed. Preserve the same fold assertion. The rotation test reached rotation and retained the draft but could not find the mode control: capture its actual failure screenshot and accessibility tree before cleanup, without changing assertions. The ordinary phone journey reached A0 through A7 in the final diagnostic record but the five-minute whole-test deadline fired before completion and could overlap the next case; allow a bounded seven-minute journey based on the observed hosted-runner duration while retaining every existing per-step wait and assertion. Source review after the 460 rotation failure shows DetailScreen intentionally marks its chrome accessibilityElementsHidden while the software keyboard is visible, so an immediate mode-control accessibility lookup is invalid. Keep the draft and keyboard assertions during rotation, then operate the existing keyboard toggle to hide it, assert the chat mode and exact session title, reopen and recheck the draft. This replaces an incompatible timing assertion with the same mode/session requirement at the point that control is intentionally accessible, and adds an input-state round trip. A duplicate delegate can arrive after the first response has completed and its prior acknowledgement was sent before that native callback registered. While a reply is pending, a duplicate must not acknowledge it early; once no reply is in flight, acknowledge the duplicate receipt to release any newly retained native completion without re-sending. Verify both phases. Run 42111899044 ordinary iPhone failed waiting for notification authorization. setupPush currently awaits the initial notification before requesting permission; a stalled initial promise can block authorization indefinitely even though native-drain and listeners are ready. Start those independent operations concurrently; do not let a late initial response act after teardown, preserve dedup and do not wait for permission before handling a response. The trace does not prove which native promise stalled on device, so add a bounded test with an intentionally unresolved initial promise and require a new device run. The same run captured a resize anchor at viewport y525 even though the first visible prompt was near the top, then corrected against that next turn; measure prompt position inside the turn, prefer the first currently visible prompt, retain fallback for promptless/very long content, and follow subsequent asynchronous remeasurements without overriding a new drag or selection. Preserve the unchanged Duo on-device assertion. Parallel startup must also survive a server-switch teardown while the initial response promise is pending: share one native initial request across bridge instances, let the currently live listener consume its result once, and never dispatch to the closed listener. Test the new listener receiving a late result after the old one stops. setupPush returns its teardown only after permission settles, so an unmounted bridge cannot otherwise unsubscribe when that permission promise stalls. Give the existing setup an optional lifecycle AbortSignal and have PushBridge abort synchronously on cleanup; a late initial notification must be consumed by the live bridge, not the cancelled one. Keep permission behavior and the existing async return contract unchanged; exercise a stalled permission plus unmount and late initial result. Follow-up review from run 42122509618: the ordinary iPhone authorization wait failed and the only captured app debug record predates that wait. If the unchanged authorization assertion fails, preserve the current debug events, screenshot and accessibility tree before rethrowing, so native rejection or a system alert can be distinguished from an unresolved request. The helper does not change permission state, timeout or success conditions; diagnostic artifacts use the existing task-only simulator fixture. Follow-up review from run 42122509618: the cold notification banner was displayed but WebdriverIO longPress attempted scrollIntoView and failed on an infinite point before the action could be clicked. Use the XCUITest driver documented mobile: touchAndHold on the actual visible banner element for both cold and warm cases, with the same 1.5 second gesture and unchanged system action, exactly-once send and scene assertions. A native hold failure remains a failure, not a skipped test or synthetic delivery. Follow-up review from run 42131652542: the screenshot showed turn 11 while the resize capture combined a later offset with earlier frames and chose turn 10. Preserve a user-scroll reading snapshot using the drag-end or momentum-end event offset and the corresponding measured visible prompt (or turn fallback); use it during a window-width reflow only while its turn remains mounted, retaining the existing bounded remeasure, tail-follow, selection and new-drag cancellation. On session change clear it. A regression must exercise a late non-user offset before resize, verify the original visible turn stays anchored, and prove a later user scroll supersedes the snapshot. Existing device fold assertion stays unchanged; this is a targeted fix, not proof of device success. Follow-up review of run 42131652542: the warm usage URL reached the scene and JS marked the usage sheet visible, but the recorded screen showed the iOS Open in gtmux confirmation covering the app. During the existing bounded wait explicitly accept only that exact system open-in-gtmux confirmation if present, then still require the real usage-close control to be displayed. Any other system alert is left untouched, timeouts and link/scene assertions remain unchanged. Follow-up review after run 42131652542: ordinary iPhone global setup waited for Appium for 180 seconds without a server or appium.log, and discarded child stdout and stderr, leaving startup failure unobservable. Capture only the spawned task-local Appium process output to an artifact and retain it on setup failure; preserve the existing server readiness wait, process isolation, cleanup and product assertions. Upload that diagnostic through the existing iPhone evidence step and use the existing CI guard; do not alter shared services. Follow-up review from run 42139938235: on iPhone 17 the notification initial request resolved, but the authorization request had not resolved or rejected by the 30 second failure capture; the screen showed no system alert. Under the existing opt-in debug flag only, issue one read-only checkPermissions query after a short delay while the request is pending, recording only authorization status and alert setting or an error category. Cancel the diagnostic on teardown or request completion; do not request, grant, deny or change permissions. This distinguishes current native settings from a missing request callback and does not treat either as a successful notification test. Follow-up review after run 42139938235: the first unfold stability check timed out while WDA calls were unusually slow; separate getLocation and getSize commands can also mix frames from different moments. Read the same element rectangle atomically using the existing WebDriver getElementRect command, retaining the same positive-size, selected-display, repeated stable-frame and timeout assertions. This reduces device round trips without inferring posture from dimensions or replacing any behavior check. Follow-up review from run 42151861243: the first fold-reading case stopped because WDA reported agent-row-%13 invisible even though the failure screenshot and accessibility frame place it on the inner screen. Require the real row to exist, verify its measured rectangle is within the current viewport, physically tap its measured center with the documented iOS gesture, and still require the exact target session header before any fold or reading assertion. This does not treat the screenshot, element existence or coordinates as successful selection; a missed touch or obscured row must still fail. Follow-up review of run 42158908662: the combined reading and keyboard journey exceeded its existing 300 second test budget while the selected-display driver was slow; Jest began the accessibility case while the earlier journey was still taking failure evidence and restoring the hinge. Separate the reading and keyboard draft journeys into independently initialized cases, each retaining the existing 300 second budget, real hinge transitions, exact session and reading/draft assertions. After keyboard opens, assert the draft and software keyboard on both panels; close the keyboard to verify the original session title and mode, then reopen to prove the same draft remains. Wait for an outstanding timed-out journey to finish its own bounded driver operations and cleanup before the following test starts, without changing product wait limits. Preserve evidence of timeout and do not infer a device pass from partial screenshots.

cases.description: native notification response queue retains a drained response until JS acknowledges it, while preserving identity, action, text, bounds and duplicate suppression

cases.action: Enqueue duplicate and distinct responses, inspect the same pending response twice without acknowledgement, acknowledge it, then exceed the bounded queue capacity.
cases.expected: Unacknowledged responses remain retrievable; acknowledged responses disappear, duplicate identity/action is queued once, and only the newest 128 entries remain.

cases.description: a stalled native notification drain must not block the initial notification fallback, and foreground recovery retries retained responses without duplicate replies
cases.setup: Mock a native drain Promise that never resolves, an initial notification and an app-state listener; also hold a separate permission Promise pending. Use identified responses and a fake reply callback.
cases.action: Start push setup with the first drain pending, observe initial fallback, simulate foreground activation and a duplicate native response, and check a pending permission request separately.
cases.expected: Initial fallback proceeds despite a stalled drain or permission request, foreground retry retrieves a retained response, and shared identity permits at most one reply. If the initial notification is absent and the first drain stalls, a later active transition delivers and acknowledges the retained response once.
surfaces: iOS Duo adaptation and ordinary-device regression

cases.description: Notification bootstrap runs before native safe-area metrics arrive
cases.setup: React Native renderer with isolated dependencies; the inset gate uses the installed provider implementation.
cases.action: Render the real JS safe-area provider without native insets, then deliver a measured inset event. Render the actual app with a ready identity and verify its push bridge starts with no native inset event.
cases.expected: Background handling starts before the event; the visual tree starts after it without remounting background handling.
surfaces: iOS Duo adaptation and ordinary-device regression

cases.description: Widget URL listener stays registered across connection and guest state changes
cases.setup: React Native renderer with isolated dependencies; the inset gate uses the installed provider implementation.
cases.action: Change the current connection or guest state while delivering widget links.
cases.expected: One listener stays active, uses current owner state, and guest or parameterized links remain rejected. Changing the client retains one listener and uses its latest client; a guest-rejected link cannot open after switching to owner.
surfaces: iOS Duo adaptation and ordinary-device regression

cases.description: The Duo simulator preserves selected conversation, reading state and input draft over real hinge changes
cases.setup: Named iOS 27.1 Duo simulator and isolated Appium XCUITest 12.20.0/WDA 16.17.1; fake server with long chat; no physical-device claim.
cases.action: Enumerate displays, measure hinge, interact with a long conversation and keyboard, close and reopen the simulator hinge, select each reported panel and capture screenshots.
cases.expected: Measured hinge reaches open and closed positions, the application window changes, the selected conversation and the same visible reading prompt survive, and the typed draft remains after fold and unfold.
surfaces: iPhone Duo simulator; physical-device and accessibility checks remain separate

cases.description: Trace search and Diff survive Duo simulator posture changes
cases.setup: Named iOS 27.1 Duo simulator, supported isolated driver and fake server with transcript and synthetic diff.
cases.action: Open the selected session Trace, enter a search, fold and unfold, then open Diff and repeat the posture transitions.
cases.expected: Trace keeps its selected session and search text; Diff remains open and both can be exited after posture changes.
surfaces: iPhone Duo simulator; physical-device and accessibility checks remain separate

cases.description: Cold scene activity includes the type and original activity expected by React Native
cases.setup: Standalone native Swift check with a synthetic browsing activity and URL.
cases.action: Build the scene launch dictionary through the same helper called by SceneDelegate.
cases.expected: The dictionary includes the browsing activity type under the supplied UIKit key and retains the original activity and URL; actual UIKit delivery remains a device test.
surfaces: iOS scene cold links

cases.description: Duo panels retain session and tools access at an enlarged accessibility text size
cases.setup: Named Duo simulator, supported isolated Appium driver, fake server; remember and restore the simulator text size.
cases.action: Set accessibility-large, use the session row on the folded panel, unfold and open the session tools; record screenshots and XCTest accessibility audit findings for each panel.
cases.expected: The size setting reports accessibility-large and the selected session and tools are reachable on both panels; save actual audit findings without claiming a VoiceOver or physical-device pass.
surfaces: Duo simulator text sizing and automated accessibility audit

cases.description: Scene links arriving after headless React starts survive until the visual consumer is ready
cases.setup: Native Swift synthetic scene inputs and a React consumer with a controlled native buffer; no UIKit device lifecycle is claimed.
cases.action: Queue URL contexts and browsing activities, drain before acknowledgment, mount the visual consumer, reject a guest link and retry an initially failed drain on foreground.
cases.expected: Scene URLs remain pending until acknowledged, the consumer opens an authorized usage link once, guest-rejected links do not become later owner intents, and foreground retry can recover the retained link. A stalled first drain cannot block active-state recovery, and a later duplicate is suppressed.
surfaces: iOS scene link handoff and app usage entry

cases.expected: The previously visible compact list returns after a round trip; an explicit expanded selection opens its reader, and a first wide automatic selection still shows its reader on folding.

cases.description: A warm scene usage intent survives a missed event and is consumed once by the visual bridge

cases.description: A history reader retains a visible turn while the window width reflows

cases.description: Notification action completion waits for its asynchronous reply without duplicate sends
cases.setup: Synthetic native response completion registry and a JS notification action with a controlled reply promise.
cases.action: Deliver an action and its duplicate while the reply is pending, then resolve or reject; release native completion and exercise bounded expiry.
cases.expected: Only one reply starts; receipt and native completion remain pending until settlement or deadline; default taps finish normally and an ambiguous send is never automatically replayed.
surfaces: iOS warm and cold notification actions

cases.description: A visual workspace starts from actual current scene metrics without blocking background events
cases.setup: Real safe-area JS provider with controlled native scene metric responses and simulated inset events.
cases.action: Mount without a scene, deliver a valid current scene snapshot and later changed insets; exercise absent native bridge fallback.
cases.expected: Background work starts without a scene, no fake metrics are supplied, visual work opens with actual current measurements and updates when native insets change, and old native shells retain their normal provider behavior. Device cold-link startup remains separately verified.
surfaces: iOS scene startup, fold safe areas and old native compatibility

cases.description: Notification permission and initial-response recovery do not block one another
cases.setup: JS notification bridge with a deliberately stalled initial notification promise and controllable permission response.
cases.action: Start setup, resolve permission, then deliver the initial action or tear down before a late response.
cases.expected: Permission progresses despite a stalled initial response, the initial action is still processed exactly once without waiting for permission, and late callbacks after teardown are ignored.
surfaces: iOS startup and notification action recovery

cases.description: A visible prompt anchors history through asynchronous width reflow
cases.setup: Rendered conversation with measured turn and nested prompt positions and a viewport containing a partially visible earlier turn.
cases.action: Change window width, move the visible prompt and its parent over multiple layout events, then start a new user drag.
cases.expected: The first visible prompt retains its viewport offset as parent and nested layout settle; a new drag stops correction, and promptless histories fall back to a visible turn. Real fold remains separately tested.
surfaces: Duo reading position and ordinary-device regression
